conclusion: All planned experiments finished; no eligible model and no minimum sufficient size established.
aggregation: Arithmetic mean and min/max over three fitted model/data seeds; ranges are not confidence intervals. Paired hierarchical intervals are preserved in decisions. No final-test reselection.

blind_observations.reviewer: Codex agent; not an independent artist/user study
blind_observations.method: All 32 predetermined full panels and central 2x crops visually inspected using view_image before opening blind-key.json. Relative preferences are descriptive, not acceptance votes. Numerical summaries were already known; anonymous per-panel metrics were not used for preferences. No checkpoint or model reselection.

panels.note: D has cleaner outlines and less speckle. All outputs thicken the original fine lines, merge icing/detail strokes and roughen parallel shelf lines; none matches clean target.
B has clearly smoother solid edges and fewer stray strokes. Others retain fuzzy halos and small branches. Masked exterior stays visually unchanged.
All recover main long lines and junctions; B looks slightly smoother, difference modest. Some width/taper detail differs from target.
All fail severely on faint detailed books: fragmented noisy contours, missing thin drawing. A retains more outline continuity but creates broad dark artifacts; no acceptable output.
All recover the straight thick vertical stroke with similar width; edges remain rougher than target. Central crop largely misses the stroke. No clear winner.
Blank target: all create faint unwanted fragments inside the active region. A appears least dark, but none is perfectly blank.

Dense typewriter scene fails for every model: speckled broken fine lines and lost tools/window details. B suppresses contrast and noise but also loses legitimate edges; others retain stronger contours with substantial texture artifacts.
E produces the cleanest diagonal stroke and least background debris; others add spurs and broken phantom fragments. E still has rough edges and changes width.
All retain fan geometry but merge nearby parallel edges and make crossing centers too dark. B has slightly cleaner and thinner spokes; difference modest and fine gaps remain lost.
All fail on the fine branching ornament: mostly fragments instead of closed clean contours. D makes broad connected ghosts; other outputs erase many segments. Protected exterior looks unchanged.
Blank image is restored almost white by all. Very faint residual speckles at enlarged view, no reliable model preference.
All miss extremely faint fine parallel lines in active region and invent small fragments. C has a larger unwanted lower fragment; no satisfactory or clear best output.
E has cleaner main outlines and parallel strokes. Every model thickens the fine target and merges short hatching/grass tips; fine detail fidelity remains poor.

All leave holes/noisy texture in a flat black bottom bar and invent faint marks on the white region. A has cleaner background but much weaker bar; D darkens the bar more but leaves more phantom marks. No clear overall preference.
Main window/roof geometry is present in all; thin pale brick outlines disappear. E has slightly cleaner window edges and less halo than A-D, with minor width changes.
All lose fine roof details and create unwanted fragments. D has cleaner main window edges than A/B/E and less roof ghosting than C, but is still far from clean target.
All keep a continuous horizontal segment but make it thicker and rougher. C is fainter with a soft halo. No confident best match to target.
C restores a smoother diagonal with fewer spurs and less stray texture. All make the thin line too wide; others visibly add branches.
Every output nearly erases the faint horizontal target, leaving weak discontinuous texture. No acceptable reconstruction or reliable winner.
Every output loses the diagonal in the active region almost entirely. C has fewer visible stray fragments, but this does not restore the requested line.
B maintains a more continuous central curve while other outputs have visibly fragmented faint sections. All undershoot clean line contrast and remain noisy; tips are weak.
B has substantially smoother curvature and fewer spurs. All thicken the line and leave some edge/background debris, especially toward the lower endpoint.
All retain only a faint noisy L shape, losing the clean solid line. C breaks more; B has less stray texture but weaker contrast. No confident acceptable winner.
All fail to form a clean angular stroke. D retains more continuity but is thick and fuzzy; others have obvious gaps and stray branches. Continuity/width tradeoff prevents an overall preference.
All preserve the Y junction but make all branches too thick. B is slightly cleaner along edges; this is a small visual preference, not a correct width reconstruction.
C has smoother branches, cleaner background and fewer spurs. All overthicken the original Y; C also extends the upper endpoint somewhat.
All collapse the close parallel pair into one faint fuzzy trace. The white gap between the target strokes is not recovered. No meaningful winner.
All lose the close diagonal pair and leave disconnected merged fragments. D has greater continuity but still one diffuse stroke, not two. No acceptable output.
All nearly erase the faint interrupted horizontal line; the intended central gap cannot be distinguished from many unintended losses. No useful overall preference.
A gives the smoothest diagonal and fewest spurs, but all outputs incorrectly bridge the deliberate central gap and thicken the target. Visual smoothness here does not imply correct connectivity.
A has smoother edges and less spurious width fluctuation. All lose the intended broad central taper and weaken fine endpoints; A is only a relative preference.

All lose the original smooth taper and create edge/background debris. B has the smoothest central stroke but larger endpoint artifacts; others preserve less smooth curvature. No clear overall preference.

blind_review.interpretation: Descriptive single-agent review only. Preference is not correctness: all models can share severe failure. No reselection from final-test images.
